finding: NHANES 2021-23 has 15 strata x 2 PSUs (df = 15); every cohort row has WTPH2YR > 0; jackknife SE agrees with Taylor linearisation (ratio within 2%).
decision: WTPH2YR for all cohort analyses and the weighted ablation; WTSAF2YR for fasting analytes and DB516; delete-one-PSU jackknife with NCHS domain df (PSUs - strata containing the domain); NCHS flags (n, n_eff < 30, KG width >= 0.30, df < 8).
alternatives_rejected: Unweighted analysis (describes the sample, not the population); WTMEC2YR for HbA1c (ignores blood-draw non-response); Taylor-only variance (no formula for kappa/AUC/standardised differences).

finding: Survey toolkit reproduces NCHS Data Brief 516 on the fasting subsample.
evidence_value: total 15.79% vs 15.8; diagnosed 11.30 vs 11.3; undiagnosed 4.49 vs 4.5; max |diff| 0.04 pp over 27 estimates
decision: Use src/survey.py (JK + KG + 3-band US 2000 standardisation) for every population number in S4-S9.
alternatives_rejected: Accept the toolkit on internal checks only (cannot detect wrong definitions or weights).
check_note: n = 2,938 equals NCHS; an n = 2,940 variant keeping 2 adults without HbA1c gives 15.78 / 11.29 / 4.48

finding: US 2000 standard collapsed to 20-39/40-59/60+ = 0.3966/0.3718/0.2316, re-derived from the 5-year standard million.
decision: Direct age standardisation (3-band US 2000) for every between-group prevalence comparison; 6-band and internal standards as sensitivity.
alternatives_rejected: Crude comparisons (confounded by age); internal-only standard (not comparable with NCHS).
check_note: re-derived in-notebook; also validated indirectly by the DB516 age-adjusted replication

finding: NH Asian vs NH White L_comb: crude -0.8 pp (-5.1, 3.5) -> standardised +2.1 pp (-2.6, 6.8); design-phase estimate 18.0% vs 13.6% not reproducible.
decision: Withdraw the design-phase 18.0/13.6 estimate; report the Asian-White contrast only as an example of honest uncertainty (both CIs include 0).
alternatives_rejected: Headline 'Asians have higher diabetes prevalence' (not supported by the CI).
check_note: design-phase figure withdrawn; numbers re-computed with three standards

finding: Insured - uninsured L_comb: crude +5.3 pp (1.8, 8.8) -> age-standardised +0.7 pp (-2.6, 3.9).
evidence_value: crude +5.3 (1.8, 8.8); std +0.7 (-2.6, 3.9); uninsured 60+ share 10.0% vs insured 33.7%
decision: Describe as age confounding (Age -> Medicare -> Insurance; Age -> diabetes) causing attenuation; never call it a reversal or Simpson's paradox.
alternatives_rejected: Calling it a reversal or Simpson's paradox (the sign does not flip).

finding: Simpson scan: 224 comparisons, 6 sign flips, 10 attenuations > 50%; 4 flips come from mediator stratifiers (BMI, education).
evidence_value: uninsured x L_A1c | age -2.8 -> +1.1 pp, P(sign differs) = 0.72; Asian x L_comb | age P(sign differs) = 0.56 (B = 100)
decision: Treat the scan as exploratory; promote only DAG-supported (confounder-stratified) flips with CIs; never read BMI-stratified 'flips' as de-confounding (BMI is a mediator / mismeasured proxy of adiposity).
alternatives_rejected: Reporting all flips as findings (multiple comparisons, mediator conditioning); hiding the scan.
check_note: grid fixed before the scan: 9 x 4 x 7 = 252 minus 28 self-stratifications = 224 comparisons

finding: In the DAG, BMI is a descendant of race (race -> adiposity -> BMI) and of SES; ExamSelection is a collider.
evidence_value: back-door valid: race->diabetes | {Age, Sex} = True, + BMI = False; insurance->diagnosis | {Age, SES} = True; minimal sets [('Age', 'SES'), ('Medicare', 'SES')]
decision: Adjust race comparisons for age (and sex) only; never present BMI-adjusted race contrasts as de-confounded; model coefficients are associations (no Table 2 fallacy).
alternatives_rejected: Adjusting for every available covariate (includes mediators and descendants); reading logistic coefficients causally.
check_note: adjustment sets verified with networkx d-separation

finding: Structural redundancy: weight VIF 95.7, BMI 97.6 (BMI = W/H^2, r = 0.99999); six BP readings VIF 8.8-11.7; TC-LDL r = 0.94.
evidence_value: BP means VIF 1.6; Tier-1 max VIF 5.9; Tier-2 max 1.2
decision: Average BP readings; exclude LDL; prune structural duplicates of BMI inside the training folds (iterative VIF > 10, BMI and waist protected; removes weight); keep BMI + waist (or WHtR, S8) under L2.
alternatives_rejected: Unprotected VIF deletion (O'Brien 2007: VIF alone is not a reason to drop BMI or waist); PCA of body measures (destroys interpretability).
check_note: VIFs re-computed; n = 5,388 for the raw anthropometry set

finding: Right skew: BMI 1.22, SBP 0.93, HDL 1.08; triglycerides 6.62 on the valid fasting subsample.
evidence_value: BMI 1.22 -> log 0.42 -> YJ -0.00; TG 6.62 (n 2820) vs 6.23 incl. non-fasting
decision: Offer Yeo-Johnson as a toggleable step fitted inside training folds only; the S7 ablation decides; triglycerides are not a T1/T2 feature.
alternatives_rejected: Transform on the full data before splitting (leakage of lambda); log for variables that can be 0 (PIR).
check_note: valid fasting value 6.62; including the 235 rows with WTSAF2YR = 0 would give 6.23

finding: Non-linearity: RCS LR chi2(2) age 57.6, TC 41.8, HDL 18.5, BMI 11.6, waist 7.1 (p < 0.05); SBP 5.9 (p 0.053); PIR 0.8.
decision: Main model: L2 logistic regression with SplineTransformer(n_knots=4, degree=3, knots='quantile', extrapolation='linear') on continuous features; linear arm as ablation.
alternatives_rejected: Plain linear logit (misses curvature); fixed-cut categorisation (loses information, arbitrary cut-points); GAM/boosting (outside HR3).

finding: Interactions with BMI not detectable: race x BMI and Asian x BMI non-significant under all three specifications.
evidence_value: primary: race x BMI p = 0.39, Asian x BMI p = 0.93; MDE Asian x BMI 0.70 log-OR per 5 kg/m²; sex x BMI p range 0.008-0.83 (specification-dependent)
decision: No interaction terms in the main model ('not detectable, underpowered', not 'absent'); the Asian BMI problem is addressed as measurement (WHtR, S5/S8), not by an interaction.
alternatives_rejected: Adding race x BMI terms (cost variance, power too low to estimate them); claiming no interaction exists.
check_note: three specifications compared; conclusions for race terms hold in every one, sex x BMI is specification-dependent

finding: Data -> algorithm table: 9 diagnostics mapped to modelling decisions.
decision: S7 cites the DAJ table for model justification; shallow tree only for thresholds and leakage.
alternatives_rejected: Choosing the algorithm before looking at data structure; using complex models (HR3).

finding: S4 self-check: 23/23 verified reference values reproduced on a clean re-run.
decision: Freeze the S4 numbers; downstream stages read them from results/metrics_S4.json.
alternatives_rejected: Re-reading numbers instead of recomputing them.
